requirements.requirement: Provide a RHEL 8.8-compatible offline DNF repository containing zsh, its dependencies, repository metadata, and the public signing key.
requirements.summary: Node1 contains 161 RPMs including zsh; repoclosure succeeds, every RPM verifies, and the metadata, detached signature, key, and zsh package remain present after restart.

requirements.requirement: Publish offline-rhel8 from node1 over HTTP on TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: Apache is enabled and listening on 8080, the firewall permits the port, and node2 retrieves metadata, its signature, and the key over HTTP. A bounded node1 restart shows a changed boot ID followed by full service and content recovery.

requirements.requirement: Sign repository metadata and enforce repository-metadata and RPM signature verification on node2.
requirements.summary: The detached metadata signature verifies against the published key, all 161 RPMs verify against that key, and node2 has both repo_gpgcheck and gpgcheck enabled. DNF imports the key and successfully performs signed metadata and RPM transactions; the policy, trusted key, and signed zsh package persist after restart.

requirements.requirement: Assign offline-rhel8 priority 10 and give every other enabled repository priority 90 or lower preference.
requirements.summary: The only initially enabled repositories were BaseOS and AppStream. Final and post-restart configuration shows offline-rhel8 at priority 10 and both other enabled repositories at priority 90.

requirements.requirement: Install zsh from offline-rhel8 and keep it reinstallable while every other repository is disabled.
requirements.summary: Zsh was installed from offline-rhel8 and successfully reinstalled with an explicit disable-all/enable-only-offline policy. After a bounded node2 restart, the boot ID changed, package and repository policy recovered, and another offline-only reinstall completed successfully.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered service, data, policy, and package behavior.
limitations: No deliberate unsigned or corrupted-artifact rejection test was captured; enforcement is instead demonstrated by the active gpgcheck/repo_gpgcheck settings and successful signed metadata and RPM transactions (cmd-d9c5803b16c845ad, cmd-f7077fa5100c454e, cmd-b46bf1044ff24589).

Lifecycle temporary-file observations cover /tmp, not /var/tmp. Final presence or cleanup of helper artifacts created by cmd-cb0751e76e854fe0, cmd-85868aab253b4765, cmd-9775c7df177e47e0, and cmd-e3c92f215dbf469a therefore cannot be confirmed.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary state-changing mutation is established. Package installation, repository generation/signing, HTTP/firewall configuration, client policy, cache/key operations, package transactions, and restarts all have clear task or bounded-evidence roles. The malformed repoclosure attempt changed no state, while the failed semanage subcommand did not alter SELinux configuration because 8080 was already assigned; HTTP subsequently worked under enforcing SELinux. Thus no identified unnecessary mutation remained or required reversion. Final snapshots show healthy package management, no failed services, and only the intentional new 8080 listener. There is minor cleanup uncertainty because helper logs, PID/status files, and a restorecon log were created under /var/tmp without captured final cleanup or inventory.
